#5512. Mark43 Named Law Enforcement Technology Platform of the Year in 2026 GovTech Breakthrough Awards

NEW YORK, Nov. 13, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Mark43, the leading cloud-native public safety operations platform, today announced it has been named "Law Enforcement Technology Platform of the Year" in the 2026 GovTech Breakthrough Awards, underscoring its leadership in delivering a modern, secure platform that puts critical information in the hands of first responders when it matters most.

Mark43's cloud-native platform is anchored by a connected Computer-Aided Dispatch (CAD) and Records Management System (RMS) built on a shared data platform, bringing together dispatch, patrol, and investigations in one connected environment. Integrated mobile tools, analytics and intelligence capabilities give personnel access to critical information across workflows, while its open API seamlessly connects third-party technologies, data sources, and hardware agencies rely on. Together, these capabilities help agencies respond faster, work smarter, and better serve their communities.

Officers and other agency staff can search across systems for information about people, locations, and incidents, giving responders more context as they assess situations and work to keep communities safe.

"This recognition is a testament to the dedication and innovation of our Product and Engineering teams who deliver on our vision every day and continue to push our platform and the industry forward."

The 2026 GovTech Breakthrough Awards recognize companies and technologies driving innovation across the global government technology industry. The inaugural program received hundreds of nominations from more than 15 countries, honoring solutions transforming how public agencies operate and serve their communities.

Mark43 brings modern technology to enhance public safety, making state, local and federal agencies faster, smarter, and their communities safer. #5511. Compass sues 15 MLSs over office exclusive rules

Compass filed 15 lawsuits against MLSs alleging they punish agents for publicly marketing office exclusive listings at a seller’s request. The claims track Compass’ earlier CRMLS suit and focus on rules requiring MLS submission for cooperation.  AI Summary

Compass International Holdings is taking its fight with MLSs over their cooperation and listing submission rules to the next level. On Thursday evening, the real estate brokerage conglomerate fielded 15 lawsuits against 15 MLS.

The lawsuits all claim that these MLSs fine and punish agents who publicly market office exclusive listings at the request of the home seller.

Defendant in these lawsuits include bridgeMLS, Bay East MLS, Contra Costa MLS, MLSListings, The MLS-CLAW, San Diego MLS, Canopy MLS, Hive MLS, Doorify MLS, Arizona Regional MLS, Recolorado, NorthstarMLS, Houston Association of Realtors, Stellar MLS and OneKey MLS.

Compass also contends that MLS boards consist of Compass’s competitors who are dictating how Compass and its agents can and cannot compete in the marketplace. Compass has recently announced that it is banning all employees from serving in Realtor association leadership roles. The firm has not clarified if this also extends to non-Realtor affiliated MLSs or if it pertains to brokers and agents affiliated with Compass, as many Compass International Holdings agents and brokers serve on MLS and Realtor association boards.

“Only the law and the homeowner should tell agents how to market a home, and the MLS is neither the law nor the homeowner. Agents should be free to compete on the marketing strategies they offer,” a Compass spokesperson told HousingWire. “It’s almost as if these MLSs are asking people to ignore the evidence that proves their claims aren’t true. For years, seven of the top 25 MLSs, covering 340,000 agents across 12 states, have allowed agents to publicly market ‘office exclusives’ without fines, and none of the problems they warn about have happened. If what we are asking for is so bad, why has it worked for years in nearly 30% of the country?”

These lawsuits come after Compass International Holdings sent letters to MLSs in early September demanding that they stop enforcing rules governing when publicly marketed listings must be submitted to the MLS for cooperation. On stage at the Council of MLSs (CMLS) Open House conference in late September, Compass CEO Robert Reffkin  threatened to sue any MLS that refused to change their rules in response to his firm’s demands.

In response to these threats, CRMLS, ARMLS, OneKey MLS, MLSListings, Bridge MLS, Canopy MLS, Recolorado, Hive MLS and Doorify MLS have filed two separate lawsuits against Compass International Holdings in U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York seeking a declaratory judgement from the court allowing them to continue enforcing their cooperation rules and policies without violating antitrust law.

The MLS defendants have not immediately returned HousingWire’s request for comment.

The Compass brokerage brand has recently announced a new broker-to-broker cooperation policy, which requires all Compass agents to cooperate with other brokers and agents, including for listings in Private Exclusive or Coming Soon marketing phases, unless otherwise instructed by the client in writing.

#5510. Kubernetes now runs containers and VMs side by side

KubeVirt’s graduation from the Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF) marks a turning point in a debate that once pitted containers against virtual machines. A decade on, Kubernetes is becoming one platform for legacy VMs, cloud-native apps and AI.

Enterprises still run much of their IT on VMs, even as AI pushes them toward new infrastructure. Red Hat Inc. is betting they won’t have to choose, with OpenShift 5 managing containers, VMs and AI workloads in one environment. Running two separate systems was never the goal, according to Fabian Deutsch (pictured), director of engineering for OpenShift Virtualization and Modernization and a KubeVirt maintainer at Red Hat.

“But you’ve also got VMs, right, where you’re running applications in the old way that we did for decades before. And do you really want to maintain these two systems?” Deutsch said. “So our vision was, how can we unite those worlds to eventually make it easier to have one paradigm to run both, all these compute workloads on one platform.”

Deutsch spoke with theCUBE’s John Furrier and Rebecca Knight at KubeCon + CloudNativeCon NA, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed KubeVirt’s graduation, running VMs and containers on one Kubernetes platform, AI’s influence on virtualization and what comes next for the project. (* Disclosure below.)

Kubernetes has drawn open-source projects and commercial providers onto a common platform, and AI’s hunger for compute has deepened that pull. Much of KubeVirt’s recent innovation now comes from the AI side, Deutsch explained.

“You don’t want to repave your data center just because you’ve got a new workload that you need to address,” Deutsch said. “So you’re having that flexibility to run it in the way that you need it.”

The CNCF announced the graduation at KubeCon + CloudNativeCon NA, seven years after accepting the project into its sandbox. Next on the list is passing GPUs, CPUs and memory into VMs, while AI is changing how the community values virtualization itself, Deutsch noted.

“There’s a lot of influx of features due to AI, by the way,” Deutsch said. “The isolation model, we didn’t get to it in the beginning, but the isolation of virtualization is helping, right, in the AI age as well.”

The project already runs on edge devices and in the cloud because it offers a consistent API across those footprints, according to Deutsch. Nvidia Corp. was an early adopter, and Microsoft Corp. is now stepping up, he noted.

“I think it’s about getting the right and next generation infrastructure into your house,” Deutsch said. “KubeVirt allows you to carry forward what you’ve got, what you invested in over the past decades, and not to leave it alone because you have to carry it forward.”

Here’s the complete video interview, part of SiliconANGLE’s and theCUBE’s coverage of KubeCon + CloudNativeCon NA:

Dual Optics, Double the Impact: Innovative dual-lens technology creates layered colors, dynamic gradients, and stunning outdoor lighting effects.

LOS ANGELES, Nov. 13, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Linkind is highlighting its latest addition to the permanent outdoor lighting category: Linkind Smart Permanent Outdoor Lights ColorBlend. Featuring an innovative dual-lens optical design, ColorBlend transforms ordinary exterior lighting into a vibrant display of layered colors, dynamic patterns, and customizable effects, bringing new creative possibilities to homes throughout the year.

At the heart of ColorBlend is its distinctive dual-lens design, combining 50Â° and 100Â° optics at each light head to create two overlapping zones of illumination. Unlike conventional outdoor lights that project a single uniform color, ColorBlend enables independent color control across its dual lighting zones, producing rich gradients and multidimensional effects.

The result is a more expressive lighting experience, with colors that blend and interact to create effects inspired by natural phenomena such as sunsets and auroras. From vibrant holiday displays to subtle architectural accents, ColorBlend gives homeowners greater freedom to personalize the appearance of their homes.

With 16 million colors, more than 120 preset scenes, and AI-generated effects, ColorBlend offers extensive creative flexibility. Through the AiDot app, users can select ready-made lighting experiences, customize their own effects, or use AI to transform creative ideas into personalized lighting displays.

Beyond decorative effects, ColorBlend also delivers practical everyday illumination. With up to 12,000 lumens of brightness and tunable white light ranging from 1800K to 6500K, the system transitions seamlessly from colorful celebrations to warm, welcoming exterior lighting or crisp functional illumination.

For smart home users, Matter compatibility enables integration with popular ecosystems, including Amazon Alexa, Google Home, Apple Home, Samsung SmartThings, and more.

Designed for Permanent Outdoor Installation

Engineered for year-round outdoor use, ColorBlend features an IP67-rated light string and power adapter, along with UV-resistant materials designed to withstand prolonged outdoor exposure.

The system supports installations of up to 200 feet, with length flexibility to accommodate different rooflines and architectural layouts. Genuine 3M VHB adhesive and screws provide secure mounting, while optional Y-shaped splitter cables and splicing accessories offer additional installation flexibility.

Once installed, homeowners can adapt their lighting to different seasons, celebrations, and everyday needs without repeatedly installing and removing temporary decorations.

ColorBlend joins Linkind's growing range of permanent outdoor lighting solutions, including Linkind Smart Permanent Outdoor Lights PatternChange and Linkind Smart Permanent Outdoor Lights FlexMount, offering consumers additional options for customized outdoor illumination and reflecting Linkind's continued commitment to expanding creative and practical lighting possibilities for the home.

#5508. Elizabeth Warren is pressing GM over its $20 billion stock buyback plan

Free daily briefing on global business news.

The Massachusetts Democrat, set to chair the Senate Banking Committee in January, cited price increases and layoffs at GM

Sen. Elizabeth Warren, a Massachusetts Democrat, criticized General Motors $GM in a letter to CEO Mary Barra over the automaker’s $20 billion stock buyback plan, according to Bloomberg. The letter was seen by Bloomberg.

Warren wrote that the buyback comes while car prices are at record highs, according to Bloomberg. “This proposal will enrich company executives and shareholders, but it comes after GM hiked its prices and laid off or furloughed thousands of workers,” she wrote.

She also faulted the company for its tax and tariff treatment under the Trump administration. "GM's decision to prioritize investor profits over workers and American families, despite benefitting from President Trump's tax giveaways and tariff exemptions and refunds, is deeply concerning," she wrote, according to Bloomberg.

Warren will take over as chair of the Senate Committee on Banking, Housing and Urban Affairs once the incoming Congress takes office in January, according to Bloomberg. Democrats took both chambers of Congress in the midterm races, Bloomberg said.

GM said on Oct. 20 that its board approved a new $20 billion multi-year buyback alongside its third-quarter results. The authorization has no expiration date and may be suspended or discontinued at any time, the company said. GM also said it completed the $6.0 billion program it announced in January.

The company had 849 million shares outstanding as of Sept. 30, down from 904 million at the end of 2025, GM said. GM has spent $29.5 billion on share repurchases since 2023, according to Bloomberg. GM stock fell almost 7% on the day of the announcement.

Sen.-elect Abdul El-Sayed, a Michigan Democrat, also criticized the plan, according to Bloomberg. Michigan is GM’s home state. “GM just announced the biggest stock buyback in automotive industry history,” El-Sayed wrote in an X $TWTR post last month. “Instead of investing in their workers or new product lines, GM executives are robbing from the future to pay themselves and their shareholders today.”

Republican Mike Rogers, El-Sayed’s opponent in the Senate race, also denounced the plan, according to Bloomberg.

#5507. The cost of manual handoffs: Where homebuilder margins slip

Connected homebuilder data can help reduce pricing gaps, contract errors and the rework that puts pressure on homebuilder margins

Homebuilders have spent years digitizing individual departments, from plan design to purchasing and sales management. Yet moving information between those departments often still depends on people. Changing a plan, option or price can require several teams to update their systems, interpret what changed and confirm everyone is working from the same information.

That repeated work carries a cost. An outdated price can reach the sales center, a buyer’s selection can be missed in the addendum, or a discrepancy can delay a home’s progress toward construction. Across multiple homes and communities, those gaps can quietly erode homebuilder margins.

Higharc and ECI built their integration to help builders navigate those handoffs. By connecting the home a buyer configures in Higharc with the pricing and contract information managed in ECI MarkSystems, the companies address margin leakage that occurs when departments must recreate and reconcile the same information.

“Most builders don’t have one version of a home; they’ve got three,” said Jad Buckman, Director of Business Development at Higharc. The architectural team maintains the plan. Marketing maintains the version buyers see online or in the sales center. Another version takes shape when employees enter the selected home and options into the ERP. When a plan, option or price changes, employees must decide where that change needs to go and ensure it arrives accurately. In a webinar poll cited by the Higharc team, 75% of respondents said builders touched two to three systems for each product or price change. Some reported touching six or more. The financial consequences accumulate. An option might sell at last quarter’s price. A selection discussed with the buyer might never make it into the addendum. A mismatch between the contract and the buyer’s expectations can lead to rework or costs the builder absorbs to make things right. “None of these costs show up as one big line item,” Buckman said. “It’s like death by 1,000 cuts.” Delays create another exposure. Waiting for information to be entered or corrected can keep a home from becoming start-ready and add carrying costs. Builders also carry the labor cost of those handoffs. Employees spend time rekeying information across disconnected systems, limiting how much additional contract volume the back office can support without adding staff. Why Higharc and ECI MarkSystems built the bridge The push to connect the platforms came from builders themselves. Customers working across both systems designed and sold homes in Higharc. MarkSystems managed pricing, purchasing and downstream operations. People in the middle moved information between them. The integration gives that handoff a defined path. MarkSystems serves as the financial and operational backbone, maintaining pricing, lot information, customer data and contract records. Higharc serves as the design and sales system, where plans are developed, options are configured and buyers experience the home in real time. “Builders don’t think about their businesses in terms of software platforms. They think about designing homes, selling them and getting them built. Technology should make that process easier, not create more work between departments,” said John Wood, Lead Product Manager of Higharc. “By connecting Higharc and MarkSystems, we’re removing the friction between design, sales and operations so builders can focus on what matters: selling and building homes.” That division of responsibility is central to the collaboration. Builders can continue using each platform for its intended work while reducing the manual effort required to keep information between them. For builders evaluating a homebuilder ERP integration, that connection between departments is as consequential as each system’s capabilities. Carrying the buyer’s decisions into the contract The workflow starts with pricing and lot data moving from MarkSystems into Higharc. That includes base plan, elevation and option pricing, along with relevant lot information. During implementation, builders validate the information across their plans to ensure homes are presented and priced as intended. Buyers can then configure options through Higharc’s interactive 3D Showroom and see the associated pricing maintained in MarkSystems. Once the buyer is ready to turn the configured home into a contract, the sales rep can create the MarkSystems contract record from Higharc. Buyer information, the configured home, selected structural options and their prices move into that record. Instead of entering 15 or 20 options separately while working with a buyer, the sales team can transfer those selections with a button click. From there, downstream processes continue within MarkSystems. Finish selections and addendum workflows vary by builder, so the connection supports existing processes. The practical change is fewer touches between the buyer’s decision and the contract record. Connected homebuilder data reduces the need to re-enter selections, helping teams avoid missed options and incorrectly entered prices. Connecting product data with operational data Connecting the platforms has also prompted builders to examine the information inside them. For the first beta customer, implementation prompted a closer review of how data was organized in the ERP. Bringing that information together with product data revealed opportunities for greater efficiency and better business control. That is a meaningful part of connected homebuilder data. A plan, its available options and pricing need to relate consistently across departments for information to move reliably. Manual processes can obscure inconsistencies because employees repeatedly interpret and reconcile them. Connecting the systems brings those relationships into focus. By eliminating manual handoffs and keeping pricing and selections aligned across systems, the integration reduces administrative work, minimizes the risk of errors and accelerates the path from home selection to contract. Sales teams can move buyers forward with confidence, while back-office teams gain capacity to support more contracts without adding overhead. Building a more connected foundation Buyer expectations add urgency to shortening sales-to-contract turnaround. Consumers can configure other purchases online and see pricing in real time. Builders, however, can hesitate to offer that visibility when prices change, and updates must be maintained across multiple systems. Connecting the buyer experience in Higharc with pricing maintained in MarkSystems helps address that concern. The opportunity also extends beyond individual sales. Once plans and pricing are validated for an initial community, that work can support rollout to additional communities. The longer-term value will depend partly on how quickly builders can bring more plans and communities live without recreating the same administrative burden. The buyer experience matters, too. Showing available configurations alongside current pricing can provide greater transparency and help avoid surprises later in the contract process. “In a market where every point of margin matters, builders need to look beyond material costs and construction efficiency. There’s significant opportunity in eliminating the administrative work that happens between selling a home and getting it into production. Connecting design, pricing and contract workflows is a critical part of that,” said Buckman. For builders, the broader question is how much repeated work accompanies each new sale, plan or community. Protecting homebuilder margins means examining those handoffs alongside each department’s performance. A homebuilder ERP integration that connects design, pricing and contract information helps builders reduce that work as the business grows. Carrying the buyer’s decisions into the contract The workflow starts with pricing and lot data moving from MarkSystems into Higharc. That includes base plan, elevation and option pricing, along with relevant lot information. During implementation, builders validate the information across their plans to ensure homes are presented and priced as intended. Buyers can then configure options through Higharc’s interactive 3D Showroom and see the associated pricing maintained in MarkSystems. Once the buyer is ready to turn the configured home into a contract, the sales rep can create the MarkSystems contract record from Higharc. Buyer information, the configured home, selected structural options and their prices move into that record. Instead of entering 15 or 20 options separately while working with a buyer, the sales team can transfer those selections with a button click. From there, downstream processes continue within MarkSystems. Finish selections and addendum workflows vary by builder, so the connection supports existing processes. The practical change is fewer touches between the buyer’s decision and the contract record. Connected homebuilder data reduces the need to re-enter selections, helping teams avoid missed options and incorrectly entered prices. Connecting product data with operational data Connecting the platforms has also prompted builders to examine the information inside them. For the first beta customer, implementation prompted a closer review of how data was organized in the ERP. Bringing that information together with product data revealed opportunities for greater efficiency and better business control. That is a meaningful part of connected homebuilder data. A plan, its available options and pricing need to relate consistently across departments for information to move reliably. Manual processes can obscure inconsistencies because employees repeatedly interpret and reconcile them. Connecting the systems brings those relationships into focus. By eliminating manual handoffs and keeping pricing and selections aligned across systems, the integration reduces administrative work, minimizes the risk of errors and accelerates the path from home selection to contract. Sales teams can move buyers forward with confidence, while back-office teams gain capacity to support more contracts without adding overhead. Building a more connected foundation Buyer expectations add urgency to shortening sales-to-contract turnaround. Consumers can configure other purchases online and see pricing in real time. Builders, however, can hesitate to offer that visibility when prices change, and updates must be maintained across multiple systems. Connecting the buyer experience in Higharc with pricing maintained in MarkSystems helps address that concern. The opportunity also extends beyond individual sales. Once plans and pricing are validated for an initial community, that work can support rollout to additional communities. The longer-term value will depend partly on how quickly builders can bring more plans and communities live without recreating the same administrative burden. The buyer experience matters, too. Showing available configurations alongside current pricing can provide greater transparency and help avoid surprises later in the contract process. “In a market where every point of margin matters, builders need to look beyond material costs and construction efficiency. There’s significant opportunity in eliminating the administrative work that happens between selling a home and getting it into production. Connecting design, pricing and contract workflows is a critical part of that,” said Buckman. For builders, the broader question is how much repeated work accompanies each new sale, plan or community. Protecting homebuilder margins means examining those handoffs alongside each department’s performance. A homebuilder ERP integration that connects design, pricing and contract information helps builders reduce that work as the business grows. #5506. Bitcoin Price Rebounds Despite Quantum Threat as Nvidia’s Jensen Huang Faces Ouster After Two Affairs

The CryptoNews editorial team is composed of seasoned writers specializing in cryptocurrency and blockchain technology. Their expertise ensures comprehensive, accurate, and insightful content for...

Bitcoin price has rebounded from recent lows as Nvidia board considers ousting CEO Jensen Huang following revelations about two extramarital affairs. Meanwhile, Glassnode data shows that 7.12 million BTC, worth more than $500 billion, already has publicly visible keys that future quantum computers could potentially exploit.

The developments put two of the technology industry’s biggest names under pressure. Bitcoin faces growing questions about its long-term cryptographic security, while Nvidia confronts a leadership crisis that could draw its AI dominance and ambitions in quantum computing.

Nvidia shares plunged more than 8% in extended trading after reports emerged that directors were preparing to remove Huang. The board is also considering an interim CEO before launching a wider search for a permanent replacement.

Bitcoin price recovered from its November 10 low of $72,600, reaching around $74,000 before easing to $73,700 this morning. The rebound offers bulls some relief after a sharp correction earlier this month. However, Glassnode has identified a potentially huge vulnerability affecting more than a third of Bitcoin’s issued supply.

According to a Glassnode update, approximately 35.4% of Bitcoin’s supply, equivalent to 7.12 million BTC, has publicly visible keys. At current market prices, those holdings are valued at more than $500 billion.

The exposure largely comes from address reuse. When Bitcoin holders spend from an address, their public keys become visible on the blockchain. Any remaining coins associated with those keys could become targets for sufficiently powerful quantum computers. Glassnode also says moving those coins to fresh addresses ends this exposure.

The concern centers on Shor’s algorithm, which could theoretically allow quantum computers to derive private keys from publicly available information. That would undermine the cryptographic security protecting vulnerable Bitcoin holdings.

Bitcoin developers are already exploring ways to address the challenge. BIP 360 proposes new transaction structures designed to reduce public-key exposure, while BIP 361 outlines a potential migration away from vulnerable signature schemes.

Nvidia’s leadership crisis has escalated dramatically after Reuters reported that its board was meeting late Wednesday to decide whether to remove Huang. The 63-year-old founder has led Nvidia for more than three decades, transforming it into the dominant supplier of AI processors. But revelations about two extramarital relationships have triggered an internal investigation and intensified scrutiny of his leadership.

The first controversy involves Alice Huang, a businesswoman whose relationship with Jensen Huang has attracted attention from US intelligence officials. She is reportedly suspected of facilitating Nvidia chip shipments to Chinese companies. The investigation has raised concerns about potential Chinese intelligence involvement and whether Nvidia’s technology reached restricted customers.

BREAKING: Nvidia, $NVDA, is now working with an "outside firm" to find a new CEO to replace Jensen Huang, per Bloomberg.The company is also reportedly weighing naming a temporary CEO while searching for a replacement.

A second relationship emerged through a New York Times report identifying Kimberly Powell, Nvidia’s vice president of healthcare. Powell reportedly worked directly under Huang, creating additional corporate governance questions.

Huang acknowledged being unfaithful to his wife in a message to employees, taking responsibility for his actions. The board’s response has shifted rapidly. Directors previously expressed confidence in Huang, but Bloomberg subsequently reported that Nvidia had engaged an outside firm to identify potential replacements.

It should be noted that Nvidia has 11 directors, with all but Huang considered independent. Its bylaws allow a majority vote to remove the CEO.

Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress has emerged as a potential interim successor, while data-center executive Ian Buck has attracted attention as a possible longer-term candidate. The timing is particularly sensitive, with Nvidia scheduled to release quarterly results on November 17.

Bitcoin’s market recovery remains an important counterpoint for all these developments. Bitcoin price has managed to recover from its November 10 sell-off, with buyers stepping in around $72,700. Reclaiming $74,000 would give bulls another opportunity to challenge higher resistance levels.

The quantum threat is pushing developers to consider changes that could strengthen Bitcoin’s security over the coming years. Nvidia faces a different challenge. Losing Huang would remove the founder most closely associated with its AI dominance, potentially forcing investors to reassess the company’s leadership and long-term strategy.

The $500 billion quantum exposure has added another major scare to the market. But Bitcoin’s ability to adapt could become just as important as its price performance.

#5504. Spotify's Ringer podcast network dropped its ChatGPT deal after fan backlash

Free daily briefing on global business news.

Bill Simmons said the AI segments on a couple of Ringer shows were not a fit because the audience did not like them

Bill Simmons, chief executive of Spotify $SPOT’s Ringer podcast network, and Spotify Technology canceled their partnership with OpenAI’s ChatGPT after fan backlash, according to Bloomberg.

Simmons told Bloomberg in a statement that the Ringer began running segments built on AI-driven research on a couple of its shows in the spring, as some rivals and leagues such as the NFL were doing. "This time we learned almost immediately that those segments weren't a fit for us — our audience just didn't like them," he said.

The backlash built in August, according to Bloomberg. Sean Fennessey and Amanda Dobbins, hosts of the Ringer show "The Big Picture," appeared on a podcast hosted by Sam Fragoso. Fragoso asked how they felt about Simmons promoting ChatGPT on air. Simmons had asked the tool to channel the late film critic Roger Ebert and predict his opinion of a movie. He also had read ads for ChatGPT.

Fennessey, who co-hosts "The Rewatchables" with Simmons, said he had raised the issue with his boss. "I don't like it," he said, according to Bloomberg. Dobbins said she had not known about the ads. "Oh, brother," she said. "That's not my decision level."

Fans cut the exchange into short clips that spread widely across social media, according to Bloomberg. The cancellation came sometime afterward.

Other podcast hosts have faced similar reactions, according to Bloomberg. Ashley Flowers, host of "Crime Junkie," deleted an Instagram post this week in which she described relying on AI to look into candidates in the midterm elections, after commenters responded with anger. In May, self-help host Mel Robbins shared a post saying she had turned to Microsoft $MSFT Copilot to get her family's money matters in better shape. Commenters reacted angrily, and she added a reply beneath her own post urging followers to be "thoughtful" regarding the details they hand over to AI.

Not every host has met resistance, according to Bloomberg. Joe Rogan, Theo Von and Ben Shapiro have delivered sponsor spots for Perplexity AI without much objection from listeners, and "The Rest Is History" advertises Anthropic's Claude.

AI companies are increasing podcast spending, according to Bloomberg, which cited ad measurement service Podscribe. OpenAI is estimated to have put $11.2 million into podcast advertising during the last three months, a jump of more than 600% from a year earlier. Anthropic is estimated to have committed $2 million in that same window, a 93% increase.

Together the two companies represent a small share of the podcast ad market, which is worth $2.9 billion, according to Bloomberg.

#5503. Quantum sensor and software maker Q-CTRL raises $290M in funding

Q-CTRL Pty Ltd., a provider of quantum sensors and software for managing qubits, today announced that it has raised $290 million in funding.

Q-CTRL sells a series of quantum navigation systems called Ironstone Opal. The company positions the product family as a more reliable alternative to GPS. Q-CTRL says that the devices can withstand jamming attempts, adverse weather and other challenging conditions that interfere with GPS signals.

Ironstone Opal tracks the host vehicle’s position with the help of sensors known as quantum magnetometers and quantum gravimeters. The sensors use variations in the Earth’s magnetic field and gravity as navigation cues.

Gravity is weaker at the top of a mountain than at sea level because the peak is farther away from the Earth’s core. The Earth’s magnetic field, in turn, exhibits perturbations at regions that have mineral deposits. Such gravitational and magnetic anomalies act as a unique fingerprint of the location where they occur. When a quantum sensor detects the fingerprint, it can deduce its location with relative ease.

Q-CTRL’s quantum magnetometers collect navigation data using tiny glass structures filled with clouds of atoms. The atoms change in specific ways when they encounter an anomaly in the Earth’s magnetic field. According to the company, its sensors detect those changes with the help of laser beams. Quantum gravimeters operate on a similar principle.

Ironstone Opal includes not only sensors but also software that processes the data they generate. It filters erroneous measurements, combines the remaining data with logs from other sensors and compares the information against pre-loaded maps.

C-QTRL offers Ironstone Opal alongside a pair of software tools designed to make quantum computers easier to use. The first tool, Boulder Opal, helps researchers calibrate qubits in a manner that optimizes their performance. It’s complemented by Fire Opal, which makes quantum algorithms less prone to errors.

“The hard problem in quantum is not building the machine, it is getting useful output from it,” said Salesforce Ventures partner Robert Keith. “Q-CTRL solves that with AI-powered control software, and the proof is already public: a materials simulation on IBM hardware that any developer can now call directly from the IBM Quantum Platform, and the first quantum navigation system qualified for safety of flight.”

Q-CTRL will use the proceeds from the funding round to enhance its software and grow its international presence.

#5502. SpaceX and Tesla merger talks are advancing toward a December deal

Free daily briefing on global business news.

Tesla's annual shareholder meeting is set for Dec. 3, and the companies have discussed an announcement slipping into early 2027

SpaceX and Tesla $TSLA are making headway in their merger talks, and a deal could be unveiled as early as December, according to Bloomberg. Such a deal would be the biggest ever, Bloomberg said.

The companies have also considered a possible delay that would push the announcement into early 2027, according to Bloomberg. Their boards and advisers are currently negotiating the deal terms, along with how the merged company would be governed, Bloomberg said.

Tesla stock climbed by as much as 1.9% to hit an intraday high on Thursday, and SpaceX shares were up 0.5% at 3:20 p.m. ET. Following its June initial public offering, SpaceX is valued at more than $1.9 trillion. Tesla is worth about $1.5 trillion.

Obstacles remain, among them the question of how to wall off Tesla's China business, according to Bloomberg. The number of SpaceX shares offered to Tesla investors is among the factors under discussion, Bloomberg said. The companies have also aimed to close a merger before the end of President Donald Trump's term.

Democrats, who will control Congress starting in January after their midterm wins, have vowed to scrutinize the business and political activities of CEO Elon Musk, according to Bloomberg.

Tesla is scheduled to convene shareholders for its yearly meeting on Dec. 3, according to Bloomberg. Musk holds about 20% of Tesla, but super-voting shares gave him roughly 85% of the voting power at SpaceX, according to Electrek, citing SpaceX's S-1 filing.

The boards of SpaceX and Tesla formed special committees of independent directors to examine a combination, Musk disclosed in October on SpaceX's earnings call. "Because I'm a conflicted party, I can't actually be in the discussions of the special committees," Musk said.

Musk said a merger would be a good idea but that shareholders have to support it. A deal would need the backing of 50% of all Tesla shareholders, not just a majority of votes cast, he said.

The two companies are already linked commercially, among other things through a shared project to construct a Texas chip factory known as Terafab, according to Bloomberg.

#5501. The Association of Related Churches (ARC) Celebrates 2026 Year in Review: 63 New Churches Launched Across 20 States and 12 Countries

ARC caps its 25th anniversary year with a record wave of church launches, reaching new nations on five continents and setting the stage for an even greater 2027

BIRMINGHAM, Ala., Nov. 13, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The Association of Related Churches (ARC) has released its 2026 Year in Review, celebrating a remarkable year of growth, generosity and Kingdom impact.

Pastors, planters and partners worked together to launch 63 new life-giving churches across 20 U.S. states and 12 countries in 2026, up from 55 churches in 2025. The milestone caps ARC's 25th anniversary year and marks one of the most far-reaching seasons in the network's history.

This year's launches took ARC's mission across five continents. New churches opened their doors in Australia, Canada, Colombia, Cyprus, England, France, Mexico, Romania, South Africa, Switzerland, Uganda and Wales. Since its founding in 2000, ARC has now helped launch more than 1,250 churches worldwide, and every one of them has brought new hope, new community and new opportunities for lives to be changed.

"Our purpose at ARC is simple: to help start new life-giving churches, churches just like yours," ARC shared with its church family. "We believe the local church is the hope of the world. When new churches open their doors, entire communities are transformed, and every church that gives, prays and partners with us is part of that story."

Among this year's launches is Neuma Church, a powerful reminder of why ARC plants churches: to reach people with the hope of Jesus and create opportunities for lives to be changed. Like every ARC plant, Neuma was made possible by the generosity of partner churches who believe in giving new communities a place to belong. Each of this year's planters has a story worth telling, and readers can meet the 2026 church planters behind this year's launches.

ARC isn't slowing down. More than 55 couples are already preparing to plant churches, and the network is believing for an even greater 2027. To reach more communities with the Gospel, ARC says the number of church plants must double, even triple. To meet that need, ARC continues to invest in assessment, training, coaching and funding through its church planting resources, so no planter launches alone.

"We're so grateful for everything God has done this year, but we're also believing for an even greater 2027," ARC said. "The need continues to grow. That's why ARC's work, and your partnership, matters so much."

ARC is inviting churches across its network to celebrate with their congregations, and it has provided videos, slides and graphics for use in weekend services. The momentum continues at ARC Conference 2027 at Milestone Church, where pastors, planters and leaders from around the world will gather to worship, learn and dream about what's next. Churches and individuals who want to be part of the next wave of launches can give to ARC's church planting mission.

"On behalf of every ARC church planter, thank you for your faith, your generosity and your heart for God's house," ARC said. "Because of you, countless lives are being changed, and we believe the best is still to come."

About the Association of Related Churches (ARC)

The Association of Related Churches (ARC) is a global network of independent congregations committed to planting and building life-giving churches. Since its founding in 2000, ARC has helped launch more than 1,250 churches worldwide by offering coaching, resources, funding and ongoing relational support. At its heart, ARC exists to see a thriving church in every community and no leader walking alone. Learn more at arcchurches.com, or follow ARC on YouTube and Instagram at @arcchurches.

#5500. Kraken's parent Payward posted earnings down 67% from a year earlier

Free daily briefing on global business news.

Total platform margin fell 12% to $487 million, while funded accounts rose 37% to 7.1 million from a year earlier

Payward, which owns the crypto exchange Kraken, reported that its adjusted earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortization fell 67% in the third quarter, according to a shareholder letter reviewed by Bloomberg. Adjusted EBITDA was $60 million.

Total platform margin, which the company said it now uses in place of adjusted revenues, dropped 12% year over year to $487 million. Total platform transaction volume shrank by 30%, landing at $353 billion. Funded accounts, meaning ones that hold any positive balance, grew 37% to reach 7.1 million.

Results improved from the second quarter. Adjusted EBITDA rose 163% from that period, and total platform margin climbed 12%.

The decline came amid a downturn in cryptocurrency prices, according to Bloomberg. Bitcoin climbed roughly 40% from the middle of August to the start of October. Its price then retreated as fears about inflation and concern over how U.S. midterm elections might affect the industry weighed on the market. Many exchanges depend on trading fees for the largest share of their revenue, and activity tends to slow when prices slide, Bloomberg said.

Payward is pushing into tokenized stocks and similar businesses as a way to broaden its revenue base, according to Bloomberg. The company has said it intends to offer onchain perpetual futures to its clients in the U.S., pending sign-off from regulators. Payward agreed in October to purchase Saldo Bank, and Kraken intends to enter the UAE once Dubai's regulators grant it complete authorization.

Payward plans to enter prediction markets and issue a token of its own, according to Bloomberg. The shareholder letter did not give timing for either, Bloomberg said.

#5499. Cisco beats expectations, lifts guidance and forecasts AI infrastructure revenue to double in fiscal 2027

Shares of Cisco Systems Inc. were flat in late trading today after the networking infrastructure giant reported first-quarter earnings and revenue that came in ahead of Wall Street’s expectations.

The company also raised its guidance for fiscal 2027, citing strong demand for artificial intelligence network infrastructure.

Cisco reported earnings before certain costs such as stock compensation of $1.40 per share, comfortably beating the Street’s target of $1.33 per share. Revenue for the quarter jumped 24% from the same period one year earlier, to $18.5 billion, ahead of the $18.1 billion analyst consensus estimate. All told, Cisco’s net income rose to $4.6 billion, up from just $2.9 billion a year ago.

Although the stock was flat in extended trading, it’s still up 32% in the year to date, way ahead of the broader Nasdaq index, which has gained just 9% over the same stretch.

Cisco has been pushing to gain a foothold in the AI infrastructure buildout that’s dominating the technology industry these days after failing to capitalize on the generative AI boom in the early days. However, its push has come at a critical juncture, as investors have become increasingly concerned over the prospects of a slowdown in data center building following the Democratic party’s sweeping victory in the U.S. midterm elections. Additionally, there are growing fears about the impact rising borrowing costs will have on debt-fueled data center construction projects.

Still, Cisco Chief Executive Chuck Robbins (pictured) expressed confidence in the company’s ability to maintain its momentum. He told analysts on a conference call that we’re still in the “very early stages of a multiyear network supercycle.” He said he’s confident Cisco’s AI networking technology is strong enough to continue to capture a portion of the multibillion-dollar opportunity that presents.

“Organizations are turning to Cisco for our trusted, market-defining technology and our expertise to help them scale, secure and optimize their environments for the agentic AI era,” Robbins added.

Cisco is also building out its software portfolio with new tools that can help businesses to build armies of autonomous AI agents that can perform work on behalf of humans. It also sells the security software necessary to protect those agents and their underlying infrastructure against cyberattacks.

The company said it’s increasing its AI infrastructure revenue forecast for the fiscal year to $9 billion, which would be more than double what it earned in fiscal 2026. According to Chief Financial Officer Mark Patterson, the company is “unlocking significant operating leverage,” and this is what’s enabling it to grow its earnings “much faster” than its revenue.

Investors may still be worried about Cisco’s gross margins, though. This has been a concern for many companies, as the global shortage of memory chips has steadily increased the cost of the components that hardware makers need to build their data center infrastructure products.  Cisco’s gross margin of 65.6% in the quarter was in-line with the Street’s estimates, but down from 68.1% in the year-ago period.

TECHnalysis Research analyst Bob O’Donnell told Reuters that the decline was unlikely to worry too many people, though. “A small dip in gross margin is not a major concern given higher memory and component costs,” he said. He added that the company’s raised forecast and strong earnings and revenue was the main thing the market wanted to see.

For the current quarter, Cisco said it’s looking for earnings of between $1.34 and $1.36 per share on sales of $18 billion to $18.2 billion. That’s a strong forecast, with the Street looking for earnings of just $1.23 per share on revenue of $17.88 billion.

#5497. Documents tie banned Nvidia AI chips to Alice Huang-linked Shanghai data center

Free daily briefing on global business news.

Filings list servers worth 485 million yuan ($73 million) as collateral, including units with restricted Nvidia chips

A Chinese company that Alice Huang founded obtained Nvidia $NVDA AI chips that had been smuggled and then put into service at a Shanghai data center connected to Megaspeed International, according to documents reviewed by Bloomberg.

Alice Huang founded Megaspeed in 2023, according to Bloomberg, and U.S. authorities are investigating the company over suspicions that it illegally shipped Nvidia chips into China. Megaspeed has denied the allegations. It showed investors an image of the facility, known as the Yangtze River Delta Project, in presentation materials from 2024, Bloomberg said.

Some of the servers were sold to Aperia Cloud Services, a Singapore-based Nvidia Cloud Partner, according to Bloomberg. Aperia acquired 22 Dell $DELL Technologies servers that were fitted with Nvidia H800 chips, a model Washington placed off-limits for China sales in 2023. Dell said in a statement that it "stopped all sales and support to Aperia International in February 2025 due to unauthorized diversion concerns."

Singapore detained Aperia's CEO that month, accusing him of cheating server suppliers, according to Bloomberg. He has pleaded not guilty and awaits trial. Aperia has denied wrongdoing, and Singapore prosecutors charged a fifth person in the case on Friday.

A unit of Shanghai Longteng Intelligent Computing, which Alice Huang established 10 years ago, recorded the Dell servers in its filings among a batch of 193 servers located in Shanghai. The company put them up to secure financing in January 2025, according to Bloomberg. The hardware had a combined value of 485 million yuan ($73 million) and included 52 Super Micro Computer servers fitted with H100 or H200 processors from Nvidia. Neither chip can be sold to China unless the seller holds a U.S. license.

Super Micro said the servers in question were sold lawfully under U.S. export control rules and that it is not affiliated with the facility. The filings also name 119 Gigabyte Technology servers that backed those same loans, but they do not identify the chips inside.

The filings gave no detail on how the chips were acquired or on whether Alice Huang had a direct hand in it. She stepped away from her ownership stake in Shanghai Longteng during 2017. Huang Yu took over as shareholder and stayed on as the majority owner through January 2026, according to Bloomberg, which cited official company registry data. That period covers the time the servers were offered as collateral.

Kang Wei, a longtime business associate of Alice Huang, is president of the data center, according to Bloomberg. Kang holds a senior executive role at Shanghai Hexi, the private equity firm that funded the project and previously had her on its payroll.

Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang admitted to an extramarital affair with Alice Huang, a disclosure that pushed him out of the company, according to Bloomberg. In May 2025, Jensen Huang said there was "no evidence" of chip diversion. Nvidia declined to comment.

#5496. U.S. won court order to seize or restrain more than $1.2 billion in crypto stolen from Binance

Free daily briefing on global business news.

U.S. and private-sector efforts have frozen more than $2.7 billion of the funds North Korean hackers took from the exchange

The U.S. Justice Department obtained court authorization to seize or restrain more than $1.2 billion worth of cryptocurrency stolen from Binance, the department said on Thursday.

The department attributed the theft to members of the North Korean military, whom the FBI calls "TraderTraitor." It said they stole more than $6 billion worth of virtual assets from the exchange on or about Oct. 29. Government and private-sector efforts have frozen more than $2.7 billion, and the $1.2 billion covered by court authorization is part of that total, the department said.

"North Korea's government bankrolls its rogue regime and illicit weapons program through cryptocurrency theft," Principal Deputy Assistant Attorney General for National Security M. Scott Proctor said in a statement. "The National Security Division will use every tool at its disposal to seize and return North Korea's ill-gotten gains."

Assistant Attorney General A. Tysen Duva of the Criminal Division said in a statement that the division and its law enforcement partners froze about half of the stolen assets before the funds moved out of reach. U.S. Attorney Jeanine Ferris Pirro for the District of Columbia said the seizure of more than $1.2 billion in stolen assets shows the government has met the North Korean regime head-on.

The Justice Department said efforts to trace, freeze, seize and forfeit the assets are ongoing. It said TraderTraitor actors continue to launder the funds through cryptocurrency bridges, mixers and exchanges.

Last week, the FBI, the U.S. Secret Service and the Internal Revenue Service's criminal investigation unit issued a Cyber Alert attributing the theft to TraderTraitor. The alert urged virtual asset service providers to block transactions with, or derived from, addresses the actors are using to launder the Binance funds, the department said.

When the government seizes assets in such cases, it typically submits a forfeiture claim to the court, and a judge then rules on which parties are legitimately entitled to the money that was recovered, according to The Associated Press.

The Justice Department also announced the disruption of cloud-based infrastructure used in a North Korean scheme the FBI calls "FaceStealer." The department said the scheme, which uses recorded videos and deepfakes to lure targets into fake video meetings and install malware, has cost victims more than $400 million in digital assets during the past year and a half.

#5494. Applied Materials posts impressive 53% jump in revenue as it beats expectations again

Semiconductor industry giant Applied Materials Inc. chalked up another strong quarter as it continued to cash in on the artificial intelligence boom, delivering fourth-quarter results that surpassed Wall Street’s expectations on earnings and revenue.

The company reported adjusted earnings of $4.16 per share on revenue of $10.41 billion, up by an impressive 53% from a year earlier. The results were impressive, with analysts modeling earnings of just $4.06 per share on sales of $10.3 billion. Net income rose to $2.71 billion, up from $1.89 billion in the same period one year ago.

Applied Materials is the world’s biggest supplier of the equipment used by semiconductor manufacturers such as Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. Ltd., Samsung Electronics Co. Ltd. and Micron Technology Inc., so its results are widely seen as a bellwether for the broader chipmaking industry. If Applied is growing, it means chipmakers are investing in their factories and presumably expecting to churn out more chips, driving growth in the industry. The company manufactures all sorts of machines to support different semiconductor manufacturing processes, catering to the most advanced silicon for AI workloads.

Chief Executive Gary Dickerson (pictured) said the company delivered record-breaking results in fiscal 2026, with full-year sales rising 21% from the prior year, to $34.31 billion. He also said the semiconductor systems business unit is on track to grow more than 40% in calendar 2026. “AI continues to fuel strong incremental demand for semiconductors and Applied has the most-enabling portfolio to advance the AI computing roadmap, putting us in a great position for multiyear revenue and profit growth,” he added.

Applied’s stock was under pressure earlier in the day following the news of Nvidia Corp. CEO Jensen Huang’s resignation, which came after he admitted to having an affair with a woman who is believed to be working for China’s intelligence services. Some investors worry that instability at Nvidia, which is the world’s most dominant AI chip supplier, could have a knock-on effect on the broader chipmaking industry.

However, the strong results brought Applied’s daytime slide to a halt, and the stock gained more than 2.5% in late trading. In the year to date, its stock is up 48%.

Applied’s main business, the semiconductor systems unit, saw revenue jump from $4.88 billion in the year-ago period to $7.99 billion. Meanwhile, sales from the smaller applied global services segment rose from $1.5 billion a year earlier, to $1.89 billion.

For the current quarter, Applied said it’s looking for earnings of $4.35 per share at the midpoint of its guidance range, with revenue coming to $11.1 billion. Those numbers were better than expected too, with the Street modeling first quarter earnings of just $4.24 per share on sales of $10.85 billion.

During the quarter, Applied made a big splash when it said it’s going to invest $5 billion in a new chip research and development facility located in Silicon Valley. It’s called the EPIC Center, and it will act as a shared R&D center for chipmakers to collaborate on new process manufacturing technologies.

Initial partners include Intel Corp., which is working with Applied and other companies on the development of next-generation transistors, interconnects and advanced packaging technologies. Other founding partners include Kioxia Corp., BE Semiconductor Industries N.V. and the UCLA Samueli School of Engineering.

Loss after tax was £451 million, compared with a loss of £559 million a year earlier. Free cash outflow was £540 million, and total liquidity stood at £6.0 billion.

Wholesale volumes grew from the prior quarter in the U.K. and overseas markets, offsetting reductions in China and the Middle East, the company said.

#5491. Five thoughts from Cisco’s first quarter of fiscal 2027

GUEST COLUMN by Zeus Kerravala

Cisco Systems Inc. opened fiscal 2027 with a quarter that should put any question about whether artificial intelligence will act as a massive tailwind for it to rest. Revenue and earnings hit records, growth rates were the best Cisco has posted in more than 15 years, and management raised its full-year outlook and AI infrastructure revenue target.

While Cisco has delivered a string of solid quarters, some investors are concerned about the durability of the growth. After listening to the analyst call, I maintain that accelerated growth is what Cisco watchers should expect, as AI will act as a catalyst for several years. Here are my five thoughts, plus the one metric I think investors should care about most:

Asked why this isn’t simply the top of a hyperscaler spending cycle, Chief Executive Chuck Robbins (pictured) cited five growth drivers: hyperscale AI, the campus refresh, the “post-Mythos” security upgrade cycle, sovereign infrastructure and enterprise hybrid data centers. “All five of these are multiyear, multibillion,” he said. “And they’re all in relatively early stages.” In particular, the enterprise opportunity is in its infancy. Using the baseball analogy for “what inning” we’re in, the pitchers are still warming up, and enterprise is what Cisco does best.

Though hyperscalers have been driving AI growth across the industry, only one of the five trends Robbins highlighted was related to that group of companies. Chief Financial Officer Mark Patterson reinforced the point by breaking down the guidance raise, noting that a large share came from Cisco’s core, non-hyperscale business. “It’s not just campus,” he said. “It’s broad-based, and the core continues to do quite well.”

The market still views the enterprise as a slow-refresh business. The call made a strong case that it’s about to become the bigger part of Cisco’s AI story.

During the investor Q&A, a data point was worth highlighting. Robbins said that of the campus switching Cisco sold this quarter, “only 9% was really coming from the new portfolio.” Despite multiple quarters of strong campus growth, the installed base has barely moved to the next generation.

Two forces will push this base to accelerate an upgrade. One is agentic AI, which Robbins said is driving “modernization for bandwidth reasons” because agents generate traffic that campus networks were never designed to handle. The other is the security fallout from frontier models such as Anthropic’s Claude Mythos — the Mythos moment. “We’re beginning to hear from customers who are attributing orders to early Mythos implications,” Robbins said, noting that European service providers are upgrading managed customer premises equipment.

Robbins added that customers “got to get the architecture exactly right.” That suggests a long, deliberate redesign rather than a buying spree, which is characteristic of a multiyear cycle.

Cisco has long been criticized for building its own silicon as the industry shifted to merchant silicon. Robbins said that outside of optics, the hyperscale AI business is “100% Silicon One-based platforms.” The P200 continues to win scale-across deals, and the G300 is now in customer labs.

Asked why Cisco keeps winning those deals, Robbins kept it simple: “It’s really about performance and power. And there’s just this whole focus on diversity of silicon in the space.” The second point is the more strategic one. No hyperscaler wants a single supplier for any critical layer of its AI fabric, and Cisco is the credible second source.

The bigger long-term play is the enterprise. Silicon One is already shipping across parts of the enterprise portfolio, and Robbins said the target to convert all of it by fiscal 2029 “is still on track.” That gives Cisco a single silicon architecture from the hyperscale data center to the branch, with cost and roadmap control competitors can’t match.

The reality is that at Cisco’s volumes, it makes no sense to buy merchant silicon. Not only can it build it cheaper, but it can also optimize it specifically for its own features and capabilities.

A theme running through the call is that AI is decentralizing. “Our enterprise customers will be running AI applications in the cloud, but they’re also investing heavily in private data centers,” Robbins said. “They want to run open-weight and open-source models in their own data centers. They want to train on their own data in their own data centers.”

Sovereignty is driving in the same direction, with Cisco extending its Sovereign Critical Infrastructure portfolio from Europe to Canada and preannouncing India. Robbins noted that Cisco is “one of the few companies that has maintained a robust on-premises portfolio.” For years, analysts treated that on-premises focus as a liability. In a world where countries and regulated industries want operational control, it has become an advantage.

Equally important is what Cisco isn’t chasing. Robbins called neocloud exposure “relatively immaterial,” adding that “we’ve been very conservative relative to the credit situations.” That’s a disciplined choice. Cisco is growing into the safest parts of the AI build-out rather than financing its riskiest buyers.

Given the number of neoclouds, one could look at them as a massive pot of gold, but they often required vendor financing. If the neocloud isn’t successful, it’s the financing organization left holding the bag. This was the case with CLECs in the Internet days. Cisco was conservative then and will continue to be.

Security has been the weak spot in Cisco’s story, so this quarter’s progress matters. Robbins said core security orders, excluding Splunk, were “the best it’s been in three years,” with firewalls, Zero Trust secure access, and AI Defense all gaining customers. Patterson said Cisco is “a little bit above the expectations that we set out” and feels “good about turning the corner.”

The refresh cycle drives near-term numbers, but the strategic prize is trust for AI agents. Robbins said enterprise conversations now center on “agentic security, agentic identity, agentic observability, as well as the new security architecture needed for the AI era.” The network is where agent traffic flows, making it the natural enforcement point. Cisco owns more of that network than anyone.

Investor concerns received clear answers. On margins, Patterson said, “gross margins are pretty much right on target,” and on supply, “we’re seeing not a lot of issues at all.” Robbins added that Cisco is growing revenue “with less headcount than we had at the beginning” two years ago.

The number I’d watch most closely isn’t AI revenue, campus orders, or gross margin. It’s the growth of Cisco Cloud Control. Robbins mentioned it almost in passing, noting thousands of sign-ups and integrations with AI Canvas, Cisco IQ and Cisco Model Foundry. Most people will think of Cloud Control as a network management tool, but that badly understates its potential.

Cloud Control is now Cisco’s core product. The best analogy is VMware vCenter, the data center’s control point that turned a collection of products into a sticky platform. Cheaper, sometimes free hypervisors never made a dent in VMware’s share because the operational control gained from vCenter far outweighed the few bucks saved on hypervisor licenses. Cloud Control is broader and potentially more impactful because Cisco is positioning it as the control point for enterprise AI, not just the network through the following capabilities.

Cisco’s numerous network and security competitors have their own agentic operations platforms, and many beat Cisco to market. However, Cisco played the long game. In my conversations with Chief Product Officer Jeetu Patel, he has been emphatic about how important Cloud Control is to Cisco’s vision of shifting to a platform company. It enables customers to manage the underlying infrastructure, including third parties, through a single dashboard.

If Cloud Control becomes the enterprise IT console for managing AI-era infrastructure, Cisco stops competing on boxes and starts competing on control. Hardware cycles always ebb and flow, so always being best of breed is impossible. Whether this one becomes a transformation for Cisco depends on whether customers run their environments on Cloud Control. My advice to Cisco is to start disclosing active usage, partner integrations, and attach rates for the platform.

My advice to investors is to start asking for them. That number will tell you what Cisco is worth five years from now.

Zeus Kerravala is a principal analyst at ZK Research, a division of Kerravala Consulting. He wrote this article for SiliconANGLE.

#5490. IEA said global oil supply is topping demand for first time since Iran war

Free daily briefing on global business news.

Observed oil inventories rose by 52 million barrels in October, the first increase since June, as Gulf exports recovered

The International Energy Agency said on Friday that global oil supplies are surpassing demand, a first since fighting erupted in Iran, as Gulf exports rebound while consumption lags. In its November oil market report, the agency described the market as "showing tentative signs of rebalancing."

Observed global oil inventories rose by 52 million barrels, or 1.7 million barrels a day, in October, the first increase since June, according to the IEA. Global supply rose by 2.3 million barrels a day to 105.4 million barrels a day in October, lifting output by 5.3 million barrels a day since August.

The IEA expects the market to tip back into oversupply during the fourth quarter, with a larger build in 2027. According to Business Recorder, the agency sees fourth-quarter supply averaging 105 million barrels a day, 1.7 million barrels a day above forecast demand. The IEA’s earlier forecast showed a fourth-quarter deficit, according to Business Recorder.

Gulf oil exports, excluding Oman, reached 18.4 million barrels a day in October, 26% below pre-war levels, the IEA said. Crude flows rose to 15 million barrels a day, or 82% of pre-war levels. The agency also lifted its outlook for supply in the last three months of the year, adding 3.3 million barrels a day.

The IEA forecasts that worldwide consumption of oil will shrink by 2.7 million barrels a day in 2026, to 102.3 million barrels a day, and then climb back by 2 million barrels a day in 2027. It projects supply will rise by 6.6 million barrels a day to 108.1 million barrels a day in 2027. That outlook was lowered because of constrained Iranian shipments. Looking further out, the agency puts the 2027 glut near 3.8 million barrels a day, a narrowing from the 3.94 million barrels a day it projected last month, according to Business Recorder.

North Sea Dated crude fell 32%, from a high of $136 a barrel in early October to $93 when the report was written, the IEA said. That price is $22 a barrel above pre-war levels. European diesel prices fell 11% over the same period but, near $180 a barrel, remained 77% above pre-war levels.

The IEA said tightness in product supply, especially diesel, is the overriding concern for the market and consumers. It warned that attacks on shipping threaten the recovery. The agency said an accelerated release of its emergency diesel stocks will bridge the supply gap until refineries recover. The IEA said that 71 million barrels from its emergency reserves release, 15 million of them diesel, will reach the market before March, according to Business Recorder.

In early October, OPEC+ core members held November production targets unchanged while the war kept Gulf shipments at 60% to 80% of normal levels. Brent crude was above $100 a barrel at the time.

#5489. Is the Crypto Market Walking Into a Bull Trap? Bitcoin ETF Records Five Straight Days of Outflow

The CryptoNews editorial team is composed of seasoned writers specializing in cryptocurrency and blockchain technology. Their expertise ensures comprehensive, accurate, and insightful content for...

Bitcoin’s latest recovery attempt is running into a serious problem: institutional investors are pulling money out of the market. U.S. spot Bitcoin ETF recorded five consecutive days of net outflows, shedding $1.44 billion between November 5 and November 11.

Bitcoin is now trading near $73,500, struggling to reclaim the $75,000 level. Bitcoin ETF outflow streak raises a bigger question: Is the crypto market walking into another bull trap?

The timing is particularly concerning. Bitcoin briefly reclaimed $80,000 on November 4 before reversing sharply the following day. Crypto has since struggled to regain momentum, leaving us questioning buyers’ decisions and whether we are stepping in too early.

The latest Bitcoin ETF withdrawals included $430.2 million on November 5, followed by another $411.9 million on November 6. Outflows continued on November 9, 10, and 11.

BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) accounted for most of the selling pressure. The fund alone recorded $269.7 million in net outflows yesterday.

The latest Bitcoin ETF outflow streak shows that institutional demand is struggling to support the market’s recovery. Five consecutive sessions of withdrawals have removed $1.44 billion from U.S. spot Bitcoin funds. BlackRock’s IBIT accounted for three-quarters of that amount.

However, institutional demand has not disappeared entirely. Morgan Stanley’s Bitcoin ETF attracted $9 million yesterday, offering a small counterpoint to the ETF-wide selling.

Glassnode’s latest Week 46 report adds another warning. Bitcoin has fallen below the short-term holder cost basis of $75,600. This leaves recent buyers sitting on unrealized losses.

The research firm also points to shrinking stablecoin supply and continued ETF selling. Both developments display that fresh capital is struggling to enter the market.

This creates an uncomfortable setup for anyone buying the latest dip. A short-lived recovery could attract retail investors before another wave of selling pushes prices lower.

Bitcoin’s derivatives market offers another piece of the puzzle. BTC futures open interest remains above $50 billion, while funding rates remain positive. This number somehow paints a clear picture: leveraged traders are still paying to maintain bullish positions.

However, leverage has already started coming out of the market. Open interest has declined, and much of the long-side leverage near current prices has been flushed.

That creates two possible outcomes. If spot demand returns, reduced leverage could help Bitcoin recover without triggering another major liquidation cascade. Alternatively, another failed breakout could leave remaining leveraged buyers exposed to further downside.

For now, $75,600 is the important recovery threshold. Reclaiming that level would put Bitcoin back above the short-term holder cost basis and improve market sentiment.

A grinding climb toward $80,000 would offer stronger evidence that buyers are regaining control, but losing the $72,000 area could expose BTC to another test of $70,000.

The bull trap argument also has a counterpoint. There is accumulation among two large wallet cohorts, while selling momentum has started weakening. This shows that some investors are already positioning for a recovery.

The market does not need another dramatic crash to trap investors. Sometimes, all it takes is a convincing bounce that runs out of buyers.
